react_result.final_narrative_text: This metabolomics comparison of control versus treatment groups revealed robust multi-paradigm enrichment of coenzyme A (CoA) biosynthesis and glutathione-mediated detoxification pathways. The strongest cross-paradigm consensus emerged around pantothenic acid (vitamin B5) metabolism, which ranked first in MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p=0.0494), appeared in RaMP ORA as the water-soluble vitamin cofactor pathway (REACT:R-HSA-196849, FDR=0.0014), and surfaced in Mummichog network analysis (MUMM:vitamin_b5_coa_biosynthesis_from_pantothenate, p=0.0445). Glutathione emerged as the most frequently recruited driver metabolite, appearing across all three paradigms — in RaMP's trans-sulfuration pathway (WP:WP2525, fold-enrichment=450×), in Mummichog's xenobiotics metabolism network, and in MetaboAnalystR's glutathione metabolism hit (hsa00480, p=0.0686). Phosphoserine provided additional support for serine/glycine metabolism, hitting in both RaMP (REACT:R-HSA-71291, amino acid metabolism) and Mummichog (MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism, p=0.0036). Coumarin and benzo[a]pyrene dihydrodiol epoxide co-enriched in RaMP's xenobiotic oxidation pathway (REACT:R-HSA-211859, Biological oxidations), suggesting enhanced phase I/II metabolism capacity. The convergence of CoA biosynthesis, glutathione homeostasis, and xenobiotic clearance pathways indicates the treatment induces a coordinated oxidative-stress and detoxification response, with pantothenic acid serving as the central vitamin cofactor hub and glutathione as the primary antioxidant effector.

Trans-sulfuration, one-carbon metabolism and related pathways (WP:WP2525) emerged in RaMP at rank 3 (FDR=3.6×10⁻⁴) with glutathione and phosphoserine as the two input hits, providing a mechanistic bridge between serine metabolism and the trans-sulfuration route to cysteine and glutathione synthesis. Pantothenic acid (KEGG:C00864) drove the Vitamin B5 – CoA biosynthesis from pantothenate pathway in Mummichog (p=0.042) and appeared as the sole input hit in MetaboAnalystR hsa00770 (p=0.049), indicating a functional perturbation of coenzyme A homeostasis. Biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859, rank 9, FDR=0.0036) captured both coumarin (KEGG:C05851) and glutathione as hits, consistent with Phase I / Phase II xenobiotic metabolism.
